messages.author: 1fb1023f38a15125
messages.subject: Calculating WAIC from "dev", or: going from DIC's dev to WAIC's log_lik
parts:
Hi,

I have some models that I have already run for a few hours. I included a calculation for the deviance in the generated quantities of my model, as follows:

dev <- dev + (-2) * normal_log( Yhat[n] , sigma );


Now, after reading the recently spread Gelman's paper on WAIC and LOO, I regret that I did not calculate a log_lik function, with:

log_lik <- normal_log( Yhat[n] , sigma );


Would there it be a way of calculate back "log_lik" from "dev" as defined above, in the post processing (i.e. in R, outside stan) so I don't have to run everything again?

Thanks a lot for your suggestion.

Judy Bennton

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Calculating WAIC from "dev", or: going from DIC's dev to WAIC's log_lik
parts:
Unfortunately, what you really need is the pointwise log-likelihood. You need to save the log-likelihood evaluated at every data point (for each posterior simulation) instead of adding them up. For Stan this means defining log_lik to be a vector of length N (number of data points). When you extract the draws you'll have an S by N matrix, where S is the number of saved posterior draws. 

The good news is that if you can write the log-likelihood function in R then you can evaluate it yourself using the posterior draws of the parameters from your model. Then you could use the loo R package. 

Jonah

messages.subject: Re: Calculating WAIC from "dev", or: going from DIC's dev to WAIC's log_lik
parts:
For the Gaussian case you can try

log_lik <- t(sapply(1:nrow(Yhat), function(s) {
    dnorm(y, mean = Yhat[s, ], sd = sigma[s], log = TRUE)
  }))

If I've understood you correctly then I think that should give you the S x N log-likelihood matrix you need. 

For the binomial case you can use dbinom (but if Yhat is on the link scale then you'll need to apply the inverse link function (e.g. inverse-logit) to get probabilities).

Yes what you wrote should work, but here are some suggestions:

-instead of binomial_logit(1,p) use bernoulli_logit(p)
-really the naming would be more clear if you swap the names of p and Yhat.logit
- maybe use 1/(1+exp(-x)) instead of exp(x)/(1+exp(x)) so you don't do unnecessary exping.
-extract(fit, pars='p')$p will avoid extracting everything else if you just want p. Same result but should be faster.

Jonah
